claims.claim: Greek and Latin languages contain two interrelated pairs of words for 'to act'—archein and prattein, and agere and gerere—originally reflecting a division between the beginning made by a single person and the achievement accomplished by many.
qualifications: distinguishes ancient languages from modern languages
claims.supporting_excerpt: In order to illustrate what is at stake here we may remember that Greek and Latin, unlike the modern languages, contain two altogether different and yet interrelated words with which to designate the verb “to act.” To the two Greek verbs archein (“to begin,” “to lead,” finally “to rule”) and prattein (“to pass through,” “to achieve,” “to finish”) correspond the two Latin verbs agere (“to set into motion,” “to lead”) and gerere (whose original meaning is “to bear”).

claims.claim: Because the actor always moves in relation to other acting beings, doing and suffering are inseparable sides of the same coin, and the consequences of action are inherently boundless because every reaction operates as a new action that triggers chain reactions.
qualifications: applies universally to human action regardless of the scale of circumstances
claims.supporting_excerpt: Because the actor always moves among and in relation to other acting beings, he is never merely a “doer” but always and at the same time a sufferer. To do and to suffer are like opposite sides of the same coin, and the story that an act starts is composed of its consequent deeds and sufferings. These consequences are boundless, because action, though it may proceed from nowhere, so to speak, acts into a medium where every reaction becomes a chain reaction and where every process is the cause of new processes.

definitions.definition: A Greek verb meaning 'to begin,' 'to lead,' and eventually 'to rule.'
A Greek verb meaning 'to pass through,' 'to achieve,' or 'to finish,' which became the accepted word for action in general.
A Latin verb meaning 'to set into motion' or 'to lead.'
A Latin verb meaning 'to bear,' which became an accepted word for action in general.

distinctions.distinction: The original interdependent role of the beginner and leader who depended upon others shifted into the function of a ruler who commands, is isolated, and monopolizes the achievements of others.
They are like opposite sides of the same coin, representing the actor as both a doer and concurrently someone who suffers the consequences in relation to other acting beings.

must_not_be_lost: The etymological shift in terms for action from beginnings to rule.
The boundlessness and chain-reaction nature of human action.
The inherent frailty of human institutions and laws arising from natality.
parsed.segment_function: To analyze the etymological roots, boundlessness, unpredictability, and relational nature of action, highlighting the historical shift from interdependent leadership to solitary rule, and examining how action inherently transcends limitations and threatens human institutions.
